newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME copper, aluminium stocks seen higher - trade.
newsitem.headline: LME copper, aluminium stocks seen higher - trade.

text.p: Copper and aluminium stocks on the London Metal Exchange (LME) will probably post a modest increase later on Tuesday, Singapore base metal traders said.

Stocks of the red metal are expected to rise by between 2,000-6,000 tonnes in the stocks report due out at 0900 GMT, they said. Aluminium stocks are forecast to increase by 1,000-2,000 tonnes, they added.
"Copper should be up between 2,000-6,000 tonnes. You may see some material come in here (Singapore) again," a dealer for a European metal trading firm said.
The volume of copper in the LME warehouse in Singapore reached 38,825 tonnes on Friday, down 725 tonnes from the previous Tuesday's report.
Singapore copper stocks hit a peak od 40,050 tonnes in the LME report on January 10, against a low at the beginning of October of 1,900 tonnes.
But another trader said any increase in stocks will probably not have much of an impact here as the Far East trade is more concerned over the widening backwardation in LME copper.
"An increase may not have much impact because part of the focus will be on the growing backwardation in the market," the dealer said.
In London yesterday, the backwardation, the premium of spot prices over forward prices, reached S$234 to $238 a tonne.
Singapore-based dealers quoted cash copper at around $2,505/10 a tonne at 0200 GMT. The backwardation here was seen at about $235-$237 a tonne.
Three-month copper prices were quoted by the same dealers at $2,269/74 a tonne at 0200 GMT, against London's late close on Monday of $2,273/76 a tonne.
Three-month aluminium prices were indicated at around $1,617/22 a tonne at 0200 GMT, down slightly from the kerb close in London yesterday of $1,624 a tonne, traders said.
